title: Base change maps are compatible with further base change
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$ and $g':X'\to X$. All coefficients are abelian groups and all derived categories are bounded below, as in [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Write $\Ex_\square:g^{-1}Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ for its exchange transformation. Write $c^D_{a,b}:b^{-1}a^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(a\circ b)^{-1}$ for the composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition].

(1) For any morphism $u:Y''\to Y'$, form the fibre product $X''=X'\times_{Y'}Y''$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $v:X''\to X'$ and $f'':X''\to Y''$. Let $\square_u=(f',f'',u,v)$ and let $\square_{gu}=(f,f'',g\circ u,g'\circ v)$ be the outer cartesian square with its induced chosen identification. For every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$,
$$
\Ex_{\square_{gu},K}
=Rf''_*(c^D_{g',v,K})\circ\Ex_{\square_u,g'^{-1}K}\circ u^{-1}(\Ex_{\square,K})\circ(c^D_{g,u,Rf_*K})^{-1}.
$$
Thus the pullback of the original exchange map is followed by the exchange map for the further base change; the intervening map is not assumed to be invertible.

(2) For every $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, the meaning of compatibility when all four corners of $\square$ are base changed is the following commutative diagram. Let $w:Z\to Y$ be any morphism. Form $\widetilde X=X\times_Y Z$, $\widetilde Y'=Y'\times_Y Z$, and $\widetilde X'=X'\times_Y Z$, with projections $a:\widetilde X\to X$, $b:\widetilde Y'\to Y'$, $c:\widetilde X'\to X'$, and induced arrows $\widetilde f:\widetilde X\to Z$, $\widetilde g:\widetilde Y'\to Z$, $\widetilde f':\widetilde X'\to\widetilde Y'$, $\widetilde g':\widetilde X'\to\widetilde X$. Denote by $B=(f,\widetilde f,w,a)$ and $C=(f',\widetilde f',b,c)$ the cartesian comparison squares, and by $\widetilde\square=(\widetilde f,\widetilde f',\widetilde g,\widetilde g')$ the base changed square. After the canonical inverse-image composition identifications, the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
b^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*K&\xrightarrow{\ b^{-1}\Ex_{\square,K}\ }&b^{-1}Rf'_*g'^{-1}K\\
\big\downarrow{\scriptstyle\widetilde g^{-1}\Ex_{B,K}}&&\big\downarrow{\scriptstyle\Ex_{C,g'^{-1}K}}\\
\widetilde g^{-1}R\widetilde f_*a^{-1}K&\xrightarrow{\ \Ex_{\widetilde\square,a^{-1}K}\ }&R\widetilde f'_*\widetilde g'^{-1}a^{-1}K
\end{array}
$$
commutes. Explicitly, let
$$
s_K=(c^D_{w,\widetilde g,Rf_*K})^{-1}\circ c^D_{g,b,Rf_*K}:
 b^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde g^{-1}w^{-1}Rf_*K,
$$
$$
t_K=(c^D_{a,\widetilde g',K})^{-1}\circ c^D_{g',c,K}:
 c^{-1}g'^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde g'^{-1}a^{-1}K,
$$
where the middle composite morphisms are identified using $gb=w\widetilde g$ and $g'c=a\widetilde g'$. The left vertical arrow displayed above means $\widetilde g^{-1}(\Ex_{B,K})\circ s_K$, and the right vertical arrow means $R\widetilde f'_*(t_K)\circ\Ex_{C,g'^{-1}K}$. If the two vertical comparison maps are isomorphisms, this diagram identifies the pullback of the original exchange morphism with that of the base changed square. Without that extra condition, the assertion is the displayed commutativity.

proof.text: Construct the extra square and the outer rectangle. By [def-pc-fibre-product], $X''$ represents pairs of maps to $X'$ and $Y''$ equal over $Y'$. Composing its map to $X'$ with $g'$ gives a pair over $Y$. Conversely a pair $T\to X$, $T\to Y''$ equal over $Y$ gives a unique $T\to X'$ using the chosen cartesian property of $\square$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], and then a unique $T\to X''$. These assignments are inverse by uniqueness in the two fibre-product properties. They give the chosen identification $X''\simeq X\times_Y Y''$ for $\square_{gu}$. This argument includes empty fibre products and makes no finiteness assumption.

proof.text: Apply the horizontal-pasting clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting] to $\square_1=\square$ and $\square_2=\square_u$, with that clause's $h=u$, $h'=v$ and $f''=f''$. Its four factors, evaluated at $K$, have successive objects $(gu)^{-1}Rf_*K$, $u^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*K$, $u^{-1}Rf'_*g'^{-1}K$, $Rf''_*v^{-1}g'^{-1}K$ and $Rf''_*(g'v)^{-1}K$. Its $c^D$ are exactly the isomorphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. The resulting equality is (1), with no exchange factor cancelled or treated as an isomorphism. The exchange maps here are the maps of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], so all coefficients are abelian groups and the input category is $\Dplus$, as required by the cited law.

proof.text: For the four-corner base change, construct the three fibre products in (2) by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The maps $\widetilde f',\widetilde g'$ are obtained from the pairs $(f'c,\widetilde X'\to Z)$ and $(g'c,\widetilde X'\to Z)$. The fibre-product property gives $gb=w\widetilde g$ and $g'c=a\widetilde g'$. For any test scheme $T$, both $\widetilde X'$ and $X'\times_{Y'}\widetilde Y'$ describe a map $T\to X'$ and a map $T\to Z$ equal over $Y$; the intermediate map to $Y'$ is forced to be $f'$ of the first map. The fibre product $\widetilde X\times_Z\widetilde Y'$ describes maps $T\to X$, $T\to Y'$, $T\to Z$ satisfying $f x=g y'=w z$, and the first two give a unique map to $X'$ by [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. The mutually inverse assignments provide the chosen identifications for $C$ and $\widetilde\square$; $B$ is cartesian by its construction. Both pasted rectangles, $C\cdot\square$ and $\widetilde\square\cdot B$, therefore have maps $\widetilde X'\to X$ equal to $g'c=a\widetilde g'$ and base maps $\widetilde Y'\to Y$ equal to $gb=w\widetilde g$.

proof.text:
Use [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-identity-pasting] clause (2) with $(\square_1,\square_2)=(\square,C)$, hence $(h,h')=(b,c)$, and with $(\square_1,\square_2)=(B,\widetilde\square)$, hence $(h,h')=(\widetilde g,\widetilde g')$. Set $A_K=\Ex_{C,g'^{-1}K}\circ b^{-1}(\Ex_{\square,K})$ and $D_K=\Ex_{\widetilde\square,a^{-1}K}\circ\widetilde g^{-1}(\Ex_{B,K})$. Step 3 identifies the outer base maps $gb=w\widetilde g$ and the outer top maps $g'c=a\widetilde g'$. Their cartesian identifications agree because each is the unique map to $X\times_Y\widetilde Y'$ with these two projections [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. The definition [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] depends only on this commutative square through its canonical square isomorphism and fixed adjunctions, so both outer exchange maps are one map $E_K$. The two pasting equations explicitly read
$$
R\widetilde f'_*(c^D_{g',c,K})\circ A_K\circ(c^D_{g,b,Rf_*K})^{-1}
=E_K
=R\widetilde f'_*(c^D_{a,\widetilde g',K})\circ D_K\circ(c^D_{w,\widetilde g,Rf_*K})^{-1}.
$$
All composition maps have the stated directions and are natural isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. Postcompose this equality with $R\widetilde f'_*((c^D_{a,\widetilde g',K})^{-1})$ and precompose it with $c^D_{g,b,Rf_*K}$. Functoriality and the inverse identities give
$$
R\widetilde f'_*(t_K)\circ A_K=D_K\circ s_K,
$$
which is exactly diagram (2) with its explicit vertical arrows. If those arrows are denoted $L_K$ and $V_K$ and the bottom arrow is denoted $H_K$, this equality is $V_K\circ b^{-1}(\Ex_{\square,K})=H_K\circ L_K$. When $L_K,V_K$ are isomorphisms, composing with $V_K^{-1}$ gives $b^{-1}(\Ex_{\square,K})=V_K^{-1}\circ H_K\circ L_K$, the asserted identification. No inverse of an exchange map is used in the unconditional equality.
